newsitem.title: CHINA: China shipbuilding exports up 95 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China shipbuilding exports up 95 pct in 1996.

text.p: Exports by China's shipbuilding industry reached $1.3 billion in 1996, soaring by 95 percent compared with the year-earlier period, the Economic Information Daily said on Wednesday.

Export of ships reached 1.6 million tonnes, increasing by 130 percent compared with 1995, with exports accounting for 85 percent of total production, the newspaper quoted the figures from the China State Shipbuilding Corporation as saying.
The Jiangnan Shipyard, one of the biggest in Shanghai, has overseas orders up to 1999 with total export value of more than $200 million, it said.
China is the third-largest producer and exporter of ships, outstripped only by Japan and South Korea, the newspaper said.
China's share of the international export market was still low, with Japan accounting for about half and South Korea taking about a one-third share, it quoted an industry expert as saying.
